premise: On a wet day Pinecone keeps her scales closed tight and Squirrel and Bird wonder what she is hiding; when the sun comes out she opens, and her secret flies away on tiny wings.
inspiration: Kipling's Just So wonder at a real thing, turned: patience, not prying, reveals the secret.
lesson: Some secrets open only when they are ready.
learning: Pinecones close up when it is wet and open in the dry sun to let their winged seeds fly.

en-US.title: Pinecone's Secret
en-US.text: {bird:float loop 0.3} {canvas:rain 0.5 12s} {sfx:rain} It was a wet, drippy day, and Pinecone {pinecone:pulse} was closed up tight. Every scale pressed down. [curious] What are you hiding? asked Squirrel. {squirrel:hop} Nothing, said Pinecone. Bird {bird:wobble} tapped her. Tap tap. Is it a treasure? A secret, said Pinecone. And you cannot open a secret. You have to wait. Squirrel peeked. Nothing. Mouse {mouse:hop} peeked. Nothing. So they waited, under the tree, {tree:pulse} while the rain went drip… drip… drip. Then it stopped. {canvas:sunshine 0.8 16s} The sun came out, warm and dry. And Pinecone began to move. {sfx:crick solo} [whispers] She was opening. Scale by scale. Wider and wider. [gasps] And out of every gap flew a tiny seed with a tiny wing. {pinecone:sparkle} {sfx:whirr} Whirr… whirr… whirr… away on the breeze. That was the secret! said Bird. Baby trees! said Squirrel. [happily] Pinecone said nothing. She just sat in the sun, wide open, and empty, and very, very pleased.

es-ES.title: El secreto de Piña
es-ES.text: {bird:float loop 0.3} {canvas:rain 0.5 12s} {sfx:rain} Era un día mojado y goteante, y Piña {pinecone:pulse} estaba cerrada, bien apretada. Cada escama pegada a la de al lado. [curious] ¿Qué escondes?, preguntó Ardilla. {squirrel:hop} Nada, dijo Piña. Pájaro {bird:wobble} la tocó con el pico. Toc, toc. ¿Es un tesoro? Un secreto, dijo Piña. Y un secreto no se abre. Hay que esperar. Ardilla miró por una rendija. Nada. Ratón {mouse:hop} miró. Nada. Así que esperaron bajo el árbol, {tree:pulse} mientras la lluvia hacía plic… plic… plic. Y paró. {canvas:sunshine 0.8 16s} Salió el sol, cálido y seco. Y entonces Piña empezó a moverse. {sfx:crick solo} [whispers] Se estaba abriendo. Escama a escama. Más y más. [gasps] Y de cada rendija salió volando una semillita con un ala diminuta. {pinecone:sparkle} {sfx:whirr} Fiu… fiu… fiu… lejos, con la brisa. ¡Ese era el secreto!, dijo Pájaro. ¡Arbolitos!, dijo Ardilla. [happily] Piña no dijo nada. Se quedó al sol, abierta del todo, vacía, y muy, muy contenta.

rain.prompt: light steady drizzle dripping through pine branches

crick.prompt: a pinecone's scales slowly creaking and clicking open in the sun, small woody ticks

whirr.prompt: several tiny winged seeds whirring and spinning away on a breeze, papery and light
